- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If true price shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50% of 30d avg), model tends to lag; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.  
- For 30d forecasts, if sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.  
- If true price deviates >5% from 30d moving average, model often misjudges direction; use 14d EWMA as secondary signal to correct bias.
